newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch lower in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slid modestly into negative territory in thin trade Monday afternoon.
Yield spreads on current coupons tightened about a basis point to Treasuries, but pass-through activity was stymied by an empty economic calendar Monday, traders said.
"Mortgages have been doing pretty well the last couple of trading sessions ... but the market is dead," said one New York-based trader.
"A day like today makes you feel like you are going to be in a trading range for the next 20 years," said another trader, adding that "it's probably not a bad time to add a little bit of coupon."
Expecting the Federal Reserve to hold short-term interest rates steady for some time, he said "mortgages, especially the premiums, make a pretty good bet."
Pass-throughs were unchanged to 4/32 lower overall by late afternoon, with 30-year Ginnie Mae 8.0 percent coupons off 3/32 at 101-19/32.

In other key coupons, 30-year Ginnie 7.5s had slipped 3/32 to 99-14/32, yielding 109 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable FNMAs and FHLMCs were also off 3/32 at 99-11/32 and 99-17/32, respectively.
Spreads over Treasuries held steady to slightly tighter. The 10-year Treasury note was down 4/32 to yield 6.56 percent.
